blocks.passage:
Managing up is one of those topics nobody teaches explicitly, yet everyone is secretly judged on. It is the skill of keeping your manager well informed, well supported and well positioned to make good decisions on your behalf — without ever crossing the line into being difficult.

The core principle is respect for the other person's time and attention. Come with proposals, not just problems. Give context before details. Summarise long topics into two or three lines that a busy senior can skim between meetings.

With senior stakeholders more broadly, the game is similar. Influence without authority comes from credibility, not volume. Be reliable. Be honest when the news is bad. Make their job easier in small ways consistently, and they will return the favour in moments that matter.

items.q: How does the text define managing up?
options: Keeping your manager informed, supported and well positioned to decide
items.why: "keeping your manager well informed, well supported and well positioned to make good decisions."

items.q: What is the core principle of managing up?
options: Respect for the other person's time and attention
items.why: "The core principle is respect for the other person's time and attention."

items.q: What does the text say you should come with?
items.why: "Come with proposals, not just problems."

items.q: According to the text, influence without authority comes from…
items.why: "Influence without authority comes from credibility, not volume."

items.q: "Make their job easier in small ways consistently" suggests influence is built through…
items.why: Inferência: credibilidade se acumula com pequenas ajudas consistentes.

audio.text:
I'm putting together a two-slide brief for the CEO before his external meeting tomorrow. The whole point is that he walks in knowing exactly what matters, without having to read ten pages.

Slide one is context, three lines. Who he's meeting, what they want from us, and the one thing that could go wrong. If I gave him the full history, he'd skim it and miss the point. So I've cut it to what he actually needs.

Slide two is the ask — from him. There's one decision only he can make in that room: whether we offer the extended payment terms. Everything else, I've already handled. I don't want to hand him five open questions; I want to hand him one clear choice.

And I'll be honest about the risk. If I hid the difficult bit, he'd find out in the meeting, which is the worst possible moment. Better he walks in prepared.

If I were him, I'd want it exactly this way — short, honest, one decision. That's managing up: making his job easier, not adding to it.

items.q: What is the point of the two-slide brief?
options: So he walks in knowing what matters without reading ten pages
items.why: "he walks in knowing exactly what matters, without having to read ten pages."

items.q: What does slide one contain?
options: Three lines of context: who, what they want, and the one risk
items.why: "Who he's meeting, what they want from us, and the one thing that could go wrong."

items.q: What is on slide two?
options: The one decision only the CEO can make
items.why: "There's one decision only he can make in that room… I want to hand him one clear choice."

items.q: Why is Sophie honest about the risk?
options: So the CEO isn't surprised in the meeting, the worst possible moment
items.why: "If I hid the difficult bit, he'd find out in the meeting, which is the worst possible moment."

items.q: How does Sophie sum up managing up?
options: Making his job easier, not adding to it
items.why: "That's managing up: making his job easier, not adding to it."

items.q: "She's skilled at **managing up**." To manage up means to…
options: keep your own manager informed and well positioned
items.why: Manage up = gerir para cima, apoiar o próprio gestor.

items.q: "He has real **credibility** with the board." Credibility means…
items.why: Credibility = credibilidade.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "I'll **___** the CEO before the meeting so he's prepared."
items.why: To brief = passar as informações essenciais.

items.q: "Influence **without authority**" means influence that comes…
options: without a formal position of power
items.why: Without authority = sem autoridade formal; vem da credibilidade.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "He doesn't have the **___** to take this on this week."
items.why: Bandwidth = capacidade/tempo disponível.

items.q: "Let me **keep you in the loop** on this." To keep someone in the loop means to…
items.why: Keep in the loop = manter informado.

items.q: "I'll **run it by** the director first." To run something by someone means to…
items.why: Run by = submeter para avaliação/aprovação.

items.q: "Come with a solution, don't just **pass the buck**." To pass the buck means to…
items.why: Pass the buck = empurrar a responsabilidade para outro.

items.q: "Let's **touch base** before the meeting." To touch base means to…
items.why: Touch base = fazer um contato rápido para alinhar.

items.q: "If I **put it to** the CEO as one clear choice, he can decide fast." To put something to someone means to…
items.why: Put it to = apresentar para decisão.
